q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Pink Book of the Railways from the Machinery and Plant Programme?

options.A: The Pink Book deals only with the procurement of machinery and plant, whereas the Machinery and Plant Programme lists all the works included in the Budget
options.B: Both the Pink Book and the Machinery and Plant Programme are lists of the stores held in the depots of a railway
options.C: The Pink Book contains the Works, Machinery and Rolling Stock Programmes, being the list of works included in the Budget, whereas the Machinery and Plant Programme is the programme relating to machinery and plant within those programmes
options.D: The Pink Book is the detailed Demand for Grants of the Ministry, whereas the Machinery and Plant Programme is the Works Register of a zonal railway

e: The Pink Book is the complete list of works included in the Budget, covering Works, Machinery and Plant and Rolling Stock Programmes. The Machinery and Plant Programme is only the machinery and plant component within it.

q: The annual plan outlay of the Railways is Rs 3,60,000 crore. It is financed by Gross Budgetary Support of Rs 1,90,000 crore and Extra Budgetary Resources of Rs 1,10,000 crore. The amount met from the internal resources of the Railways is:

options.A: Rs 60,000 crore
options.B: Rs 50,000 crore
options.C: Rs 70,000 crore
options.D: Rs 80,000 crore

e: Internal resources = Plan outlay - Gross Budgetary Support - Extra Budgetary Resources = 360000 - 190000 - 110000 = Rs 60,000 crore.

q: The charges of a project organisation for general administration and supervision are common both to a new line under construction and to open-line works served by the same organisation. In the accounts, such common service charges are allocated between Capital and Revenue:

options.A: Equally in all cases, half to Capital and half to Revenue
options.B: Entirely to Capital, as the organisation was set up for the new line
options.C: Entirely to Revenue, as administration is a revenue charge
options.D: In the proportions prescribed in the rules and codes for such allocation

e: Common general supervision and administration charges of a project organisation serving both construction and open line are allocated between Capital and Revenue in the proportions prescribed in the codes, not arbitrarily equally or wholly to one side.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 11,50,000 crore and its primary deficit for the year is Rs 7,90,000 crore. The interest payments of the Government during the year amount to:

options.A: Rs 3,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 3,60,000 crore
options.C: Rs 4,20,000 crore
options.D: Rs 7,90,000 crore

e: Interest payments = Fiscal deficit - Primary deficit = Rs 11,50,000 crore - Rs 7,90,000 crore = Rs 3,60,000 crore, since primary deficit is fiscal deficit excluding interest.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an Advice of Payment from a Cash Remittance Note in railway accounts?

options.A: An Advice of Payment is sent by an accounting unit which has made a payment on behalf of another unit, to intimate the payment so that the other unit can bring it to account, whereas a Cash Remittance Note accompanies the cash remitted by a station to the Cash Office or the bank
options.B: An Advice of Payment accompanies the cash remitted by a station, whereas a Cash Remittance Note intimates a payment made on behalf of another Ministry
options.C: Both the documents are issued by the Reserve Bank of India to intimate the credits given to the Railways
options.D: An Advice of Payment intimates a debit raised by one railway against another through the Traffic Book, whereas a Cash Remittance Note is issued by the Railway Board

e: An Advice of Payment intimates a payment made by one accounting unit on behalf of another so the latter can account for it. A Cash Remittance Note accompanies cash remitted by a station to the Cash Office or bank.

q: The earnings originated and collected by a zonal railway for a period are Rs 4,200 crore, while the earnings apportioned to the railway for the same period, after apportionment of through-traffic earnings, are Rs 4,650 crore. The net result of apportionment for the railway is:

options.A: A net loss of Rs 450 crore on apportionment
options.B: A net gain of Rs 8,850 crore on apportionment
options.C: A net gain of Rs 450 crore on apportionment
options.D: No gain or loss, apportionment never affecting a railway's own earnings

e: Net result of apportionment = Apportioned earnings - Originated earnings = Rs 4,650 crore - Rs 4,200 crore = a net gain of Rs 450 crore to the railway.

q: The recovery of the principal of a House Building Advance, and of other loans advanced by the Government to its servants, is treated in the Government accounts as:

options.A: A revenue receipt of the Government
options.B: A receipt credited to the Public Account of India
options.C: A Sundry Other Earning of the Railways
options.D: A non-debt capital receipt, by way of recovery of loans and advances

e: Recovery of principal of House Building Advance and other Government loans to servants is a non-debt capital receipt, shown as recovery of loans and advances. It is not revenue, as it realises an existing asset.

q: The opening credit balance under the head 'Demands Payable' of a railway is Rs 4,25,000. During the year, amounts of Rs 11,75,000 are credited to the head for goods and services received and the closing credit balance under the head is Rs 3,50,000. The payments made during the year, by debit to the head, amount to:
e: Payments = Opening credit + Credits during year - Closing credit = 425000 + 1175000 - 350000 = Rs 12,50,000 by debit to Demands Payable.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Subsidiary Books from the General Books of a railway?

options.A: Both the Subsidiary Books and the General Books are rendered monthly to the Railway Board as the Account Current
options.B: The Subsidiary Books contain the classified postings under the heads of account, whereas the General Books record the cash transactions at the stations in detail
options.C: The Subsidiary Books are the books in which the transactions are first recorded in detail, such as the Main Cash Book and the Journal Book, whereas the General Books, of which the Ledger is the principal book, contain the transactions posted in classified form under the heads of account from the classified summaries of the subsidiary books
options.D: The Subsidiary Books are maintained only in the Railway Board's office, whereas the General Books are maintained at the stations

e: Subsidiary Books are books of first detailed record, such as the Main Cash Book and Journal Book. General Books, principally the Ledger, contain classified postings under heads of account made from summaries of the subsidiary books.

q: A zonal railway makes a payment on behalf of a Pay and Accounts Office of another Ministry of the Government of India, the settlement of the transaction with that Ministry being awaited. Pending settlement, the amount is passed through the suspense head:

options.A: PAO Suspense
options.B: AG Suspense
options.C: Reserve Bank Suspense
options.D: PSB Suspense

e: A payment made on behalf of a Pay and Accounts Office of another Central Ministry, pending settlement with that Ministry, is passed through PAO Suspense.

q: The Block Account of a railway at the commencement of a year stands at Rs 52,000 crore. During the year, assets of the original cost of Rs 350 crore are sold and removed from the Block, and the Block Account at the close of the year stands at Rs 54,650 crore. The capital outlay incurred during the year is:

options.A: Rs 2,650 crore
options.B: Rs 3,350 crore
options.C: Rs 2,300 crore
options.D: Rs 3,000 crore

e: Capital outlay = Closing Block - Opening Block + Cost of assets sold and removed = 54650 - 52000 + 350 = Rs 3,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Main Cash Book from the Classified Abstract of a railway?

options.A: The Main Cash Book is the head-wise monthly summary from which the General Books are posted, whereas the Classified Abstract records the cash transactions of the Cash and Pay Office
options.B: The Main Cash Book records, in chronological order, all the cash receipts and payments effected through the Cash and Pay Office, whereas the Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary of transactions prepared from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted
options.C: Both the Main Cash Book and the Classified Abstract are rendered monthly to the Railway Board as the Account Current of the railway
options.D: The Main Cash Book is maintained in the Traffic Accounts Office, whereas the Classified Abstract is maintained at the stations

e: The Main Cash Book records Cash and Pay Office cash transactions chronologically. The Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary prepared from subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted.

q: The Effective Capital Expenditure of the Government for a year is Rs 4,20,000 crore, which includes grants-in-aid of Rs 70,000 crore given during the year for the creation of capital assets. The capital expenditure of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 3,50,000 crore
options.B: Rs 4,90,000 crore
options.C: Rs 3,00,000 crore
options.D: Rs 4,20,000 crore

e: Effective Capital Expenditure = Capital expenditure + Grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets, so capital expenditure = 420000 - 70000 = Rs 3,50,000 crore.

q: An executive department proposes to frame its estimates of expenditure after netting off the recoveries expected from outside parties for services to be rendered by the Railways, so that only the net amount is provided in the Budget. The correct position under the principles of Government budgeting is that:

options.A: The proposal is in order, net budgeting being the prescribed basis for all estimates
options.B: The proposal is in order only for works financed from the Development Fund
options.C: The estimates of expenditure are framed in gross terms, without netting off the related receipts
options.D: The netting is permissible with the sanction of the General Manager alone

e: Government budgeting is on a gross basis: estimates of expenditure are framed in full without netting off expected recoveries or receipts, which are accounted for separately.

q: The opening balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense' of a railway, representing the cost of jobs in progress in its workshops, is Rs 95 lakh. During the year, completed jobs of Rs 505 lakh are transferred out of the head and the closing balance under the head is Rs 70 lakh. The amount charged to the head during the year for jobs undertaken is:

options.A: Rs 410 lakh
options.B: Rs 480 lakh
options.C: Rs 530 lakh
options.D: Rs 600 lakh

e: Amount charged = Closing balance - Opening balance + Completed jobs transferred out = 70 - 95 + 505 = Rs 480 lakh under Manufacturing Suspense.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Earnings Budget from the Capital Budget of the Railways?

options.A: Both the Earnings Budget and the Capital Budget list the works included in the Works Programme for the year
options.B: The Earnings Budget provides for the capital outlay on works, whereas the Capital Budget estimates the traffic receipts of the year
options.C: The Earnings Budget is framed by the Railway Board alone, whereas the Capital Budget is framed on the anticipated volume of traffic and the fares and rates in force
options.D: The Earnings Budget contains the estimates of the earnings of the Railways, framed on the anticipated volume of passenger and goods traffic and the fares and rates expected to be in force, whereas the Capital Budget contains the provision for the capital outlay on the works included in the Works Programme

e: The Earnings Budget estimates traffic earnings from anticipated traffic volume and fares and rates in force. The Capital Budget provides capital outlay for works in the Works Programme.

q: During the same financial year, the Accounts Office finds that an item of pay, amounting to Rs 42,000, has been booked under a wrong head of account. The error of classification is corrected in the books through:

options.A: A Transfer Entry Order, giving effect to a journal (transfer) entry between the heads concerned
options.B: A fresh Demand for Grant presented to Parliament
options.C: A permanent booking under a suspense head
options.D: The Budget Estimates of the following year alone

e: A classification error detected within the same financial year is corrected by a journal transfer entry authorised through a Transfer Entry Order between the heads concerned.

q: The opening debit balance under the suspense head 'Demands Recoverable' of a railway is Rs 3,15,000. During the year, amounts of Rs 8,85,000 are debited to the head for services rendered to outside parties and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 2,70,000. The amount realised from the parties during the year, by credit to the head, is:
e: Realised = Opening debit + Debits during year - Closing debit = 315000 + 885000 - 270000 = Rs 9,30,000 credited to Demands Recoverable.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Suspense Register from the Works Register maintained in the Accounts Office?

options.A: The Suspense Register records the progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work, whereas the Works Register watches the outstanding suspense items
options.B: The Suspense Register watches the outstanding items under each suspense head, whereas the Works Register records, work-wise, the sanctions, budget allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work
options.C: Both the registers record only the balances under the debt heads of account
options.D: The Suspense Register is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Works Register is maintained at the stations

e: The Suspense Register watches outstanding items under each suspense head for clearance. The Works Register records work-wise sanctions, allotments and progressive expenditure on each sanctioned work.

q: The gross earnings of a zonal railway for a year are Rs 6,800 crore and its total working expenses, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, are Rs 7,140 crore. The net revenue of the railway for the year is:

options.A: A shortfall of Rs 340 crore
options.B: A surplus of Rs 340 crore
options.C: A surplus of Rs 13,940 crore
options.D: A shortfall of Rs 680 crore

e: Net revenue = Gross earnings - Total working expenses = Rs 6,800 crore - Rs 7,140 crore = a shortfall of Rs 340 crore, expenses exceeding earnings.

q: In preparing the schedules supporting the Balance Sheet of a railway, a clerk proposes to show the accumulated balances of the State Railway Provident Fund under the suspense heads. The correct grouping of these balances in the railway accounts is under:

options.A: The revenue heads
options.B: The capital heads
options.C: The remittance heads
options.D: The Debt heads

e: Provident Fund balances such as the State Railway Provident Fund are Government liabilities held in trust, grouped under Debt heads in the Balance Sheet schedules, not under suspense, revenue or remittance heads.

q: The total expenditure of the Government for a year is Rs 42,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 25,00,000 crore and its fiscal deficit for the year is Rs 15,00,000 crore. The non-debt capital receipts of the Government for the year are:

options.A: Rs 17,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 2,00,000 crore
options.C: Rs 10,00,000 crore
options.D: Rs 5,00,000 crore

e: Non-debt capital receipts = Total expenditure - Revenue receipts - Fiscal deficit = 4200000 - 2500000 - 1500000 = Rs 2,00,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Revenue Account from the Finance Accounts in the annual accounts of the Railways?

options.A: Both the Revenue Account and the Finance Accounts exhibit only the assets and liabilities of the Railways
options.B: The Revenue Account presents the total receipts and disbursements under the major heads, whereas the Finance Accounts exhibit the working results of the year
options.C: The Revenue Account exhibits the results of the working of the Railways for the year, in the shape of earnings, working expenses and the surplus or shortfall, whereas the Finance Accounts present the total receipts and disbursements of the year under the respective major heads of account
options.D: The Revenue Account is the monthly account rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Finance Accounts are compiled at the stations

e: The Revenue Account shows working results: earnings, working expenses and surplus or shortfall. The Finance Accounts present total receipts and disbursements of the year under the respective major heads.

q: In a year in which the total working expenses of a zonal railway exceed its gross earnings, the Operating Ratio of the railway for the year will be:

options.A: More than 100 per cent
options.B: Exactly 100 per cent
options.C: Less than 50 per cent
options.D: Nil, as the ratio is not worked out for such a year

e: Operating Ratio = Working expenses x 100 / Gross earnings. If expenses exceed earnings, the ratio necessarily exceeds 100 per cent.

q: The opening debit balance under the remittance head 'Remittances into Banks' of a railway is Rs 95,000. During the month, remittances of Rs 12,35,000 are made into the bank and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 1,10,000. The amount for which the bank has given credit during the month is:
e: Bank credit = Opening balance + Remittances - Closing balance = 95000 + 1235000 - 110000 = Rs 12,20,000 under Remittances into Banks.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Ledger of a railway from its monthly Account Current?

options.A: The Ledger is the monthly account rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Account Current is a General Book of the railway
options.B: The Ledger is a General Book in which the transactions are posted in classified form under the heads of account, whereas the Account Current is the monthly account of the railway compiled from the General Books and rendered to the Railway Board
options.C: Both the Ledger and the Account Current are subsidiary books in which transactions are first recorded in detail
options.D: The Ledger is maintained at the stations, whereas the Account Current is maintained in the Cash and Pay Office

e: The Ledger is a General Book with classified postings under heads of account. The Account Current is the monthly account compiled from the General Books and rendered by the railway to the Railway Board.

q: Expenditure of Rs 620 crore has been incurred on a work up to the end of the previous year. An outlay of Rs 180 crore is provided for the work in the current year and the throw-forward of the work at the end of the current year will be Rs 150 crore. The sanctioned cost of the work is:

options.A: Rs 800 crore
options.B: Rs 770 crore
options.C: Rs 950 crore
options.D: Rs 330 crore

e: Sanctioned cost = Past expenditure + Current outlay + Throw-forward = 620 + 180 + 150 = Rs 950 crore.

q: The Government disinvests a part of its shareholding in a railway public sector undertaking and realises the proceeds during the year. In the Government accounts, these proceeds are classified as:

options.A: Non-debt capital receipts, as they reduce the assets of the Government without creating a liability for repayment
options.B: Revenue receipts of the Government
options.C: Debt capital receipts, as they create a liability for repayment
options.D: Receipts credited to the Public Account of India

e: Disinvestment proceeds realise Government shareholding without creating any repayment liability, so they are non-debt capital receipts, not revenue receipts or debt receipts.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Traffic Book from the monthly Account Current of a zonal railway?

options.A: The Traffic Book is the monthly account of the whole railway rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Account Current deals with the apportionment of earnings
options.B: Both the Traffic Book and the Account Current are compiled from the General Books of the railway
options.C: The Traffic Book is maintained in the Cash and Pay Office, whereas the Account Current is compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office from the station balance sheets
options.D: The Traffic Book is principally concerned with the apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the railways concerned and the adjustment of the results thereof, whereas the Account Current is the monthly account of the railway rendered to the Railway Board and compiled from its General Books

e: The Traffic Book deals principally with apportionment of through-traffic earnings among the railways concerned and adjustment of the results. The Account Current is the monthly account to the Railway Board compiled from the General Books.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 24,000 include terminal charges of Rs 3,000, which are retained by Railway P, the railway rendering the terminal services. The balance is apportioned between Railway P, over which the traffic travels 700 km, and Railway Q, over which it travels 500 km, in proportion to the distance travelled. The total amount which falls to the share of Railway P, including the terminal charges retained by it, is:
e: Apportionable balance = Rs 24,000 - Rs 3,000 terminals = Rs 21,000. Railway P distance share = 700 / 1200 x 21000 = Rs 12,250, plus terminals Rs 3,000 = Rs 15,250 in total.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Station Balance Sheet from the monthly Account Current of a zonal railway?

options.A: The Station Balance Sheet is the monthly account of the whole railway rendered to the Railway Board, whereas the Account Current is rendered by each station
options.B: Both the documents are compiled in the Traffic Accounts Office for the apportionment of earnings among the railways
options.C: The Station Balance Sheet is the monthly statement rendered by a station to the Traffic Accounts Office, accounting for all the traffic transactions of the station and showing the balance due from the station, whereas the Account Current is the monthly account of the railway as a whole, rendered to the Railway Board
options.D: The Station Balance Sheet is prepared from the General Books of the railway, whereas the Account Current is prepared at the stations

e: The Station Balance Sheet is the monthly statement of a station to the Traffic Accounts Office accounting for its traffic transactions and balance due. The Account Current is the account of the railway as a whole rendered to the Railway Board.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Debt Service Fund from the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Debt Service Fund is intended to provide a cushion for meeting the debt-service obligations of the Railways, arising out of market borrowings, in years when their revenues are inadequate, whereas the Development Fund is used for passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvement works
options.B: Both the funds are used only for the renewal and replacement of railway assets
options.C: The Debt Service Fund is used for passenger amenities, whereas the Development Fund services the market borrowings of the Railways
options.D: The Debt Service Fund is credited with the safety surcharge on passenger fares, whereas the Development Fund is credited with market borrowings

e: The Debt Service Fund cushions debt-service obligations on market borrowings in years of inadequate revenue. The Development Fund finances passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvement works.

q: The revenue deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 3,10,000 crore and its Effective Revenue Deficit for the year is Rs 2,55,000 crore. The grants-in-aid given during the year for the creation of capital assets amount to:

options.A: Rs 50,000 crore
options.B: Rs 60,000 crore
options.C: Rs 5,65,000 crore
options.D: Rs 55,000 crore

e: Effective Revenue Deficit = Revenue deficit - Grants for creation of capital assets, so grants = 310000 - 255000 = Rs 55,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Liability Register from the Debt Head Report of a railway?

options.A: The Liability Register shows the balances under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, whereas the Debt Head Report records the commitments incurred against a grant
options.B: Both the Liability Register and the Debt Head Report record only the progressive expenditure on sanctioned works
options.C: The Liability Register is rendered monthly to the Railway Board, whereas the Debt Head Report is maintained at the stations
options.D: The Liability Register records the commitments and liabilities incurred against a grant, so that they do not exceed the budget allotment available for the purpose, whereas the Debt Head Report shows the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads of account

e: The Liability Register records commitments and liabilities against a grant to keep them within allotment. The Debt Head Report shows outstanding balances under debt, suspense and remittance heads.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the preparation of the Revised Estimates of a zonal railway at the September review?

options.A: The Accounts Department scrutinises the proposals — the executive departments frame their revised proposals — the actuals of the first five months are compiled — the estimates are consolidated and submitted
options.B: The estimates are consolidated and submitted — the actuals of the first five months are compiled — the Accounts Department scrutinises the proposals — the executive departments frame their proposals
options.C: The actuals of the first five months are compiled — the executive departments frame their revised proposals on that basis — the proposals are scrutinised by the Accounts Department — the estimates are consolidated and submitted for adoption in the Budget
options.D: The executive departments frame their proposals — the estimates are consolidated and submitted — the actuals of the first five months are compiled thereafter — the Accounts Department scrutinises the sanctioned Budget

e: Correct sequence: compile actuals of the first five months, executives frame revised proposals on that basis, Accounts scrutinises them, and the estimates are consolidated and submitted for adoption in the Budget.

q: The opening debit balance under 'Stores Suspense' of a railway is Rs 280 lakh. During the year, stores of Rs 1,020 lakh are issued from stock and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 340 lakh. The value of the stores received into stock during the year is:

options.A: Rs 960 lakh
options.B: Rs 1,140 lakh
options.C: Rs 1,020 lakh
options.D: Rs 1,080 lakh

e: Stores received = Closing balance - Opening balance + Stores issued = 340 - 280 + 1020 = Rs 1,080 lakh under Stores Suspense.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'economy cut' motion from a 'token cut' motion moved on a Demand for Grant in the Lok Sabha?

options.A: An economy cut proposes that the Demand be reduced by a specified amount in order to effect economy in the expenditure covered by it, whereas a token cut proposes a reduction of Rs 100 in order to ventilate a specific grievance
options.B: An economy cut proposes that the Demand be reduced to Re 1 in order to express disapproval of the policy underlying it, whereas a token cut proposes a reduction by a specified amount in order to effect economy
options.C: An economy cut is moved only in respect of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India, whereas a token cut is moved only in respect of voted expenditure
options.D: An economy cut is voted by the Lok Sabha as a whole, whereas a token cut is decided by the Departmentally Related Standing Committee on Railways

e: An economy cut seeks reduction by a specified amount to effect economy in the expenditure. A token cut seeks a reduction of Rs 100 only to ventilate a specific grievance; a policy cut reduces the Demand to Re 1.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the Committee.
2. The Chairman of the Estimates Committee is appointed by the Speaker of the Lok Sabha from amongst the members of the Committee.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. The Chairmen of both the Public Accounts Committee and the Estimates Committee are appointed by the Speaker from amongst the Lok Sabha members of the respective Committee.

q: The total working expenses of a zonal railway for a year, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund, are Rs 8,280 crore and its Operating Ratio for the year is 90 per cent. The gross earnings of the railway for the year are:

options.A: Rs 7,452 crore
options.B: Rs 9,200 crore
options.C: Rs 8,280 crore
options.D: Rs 10,120 crore

e: Gross earnings = Total working expenses / Operating Ratio = Rs 8,280 crore / 90 per cent = Rs 9,200 crore.

q: During a day, a station collects charges for parcels booked, charges for the carriage of postal mails and receipts from the sale of platform tickets. Taken together, these collections are classified in the railway accounts under:

options.A: Goods earnings
options.B: Passenger earnings
options.C: Sundry Other Earnings
options.D: Other Coaching Earnings

e: Parcels charges, postal mail charges and platform ticket receipts are all coaching earnings other than passenger fares, so together they are classified under Other Coaching Earnings.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 21,000 are apportioned between Railway P and Railway Q in proportion to the distance travelled over each railway. Railway P, over which the traffic travels 800 km, receives Rs 12,000 as its share. The distance travelled over Railway Q is:

options.A: 750 km
options.B: 450 km
options.C: 900 km
options.D: 600 km

e: Railway P rate = Rs 12,000 / 800 km = Rs 15 per km. Railway Q share = Rs 21,000 - Rs 12,000 = Rs 9,000, so distance over Q = 9000 / 15 = 600 km.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Railway Pension Fund from the Capital Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The Pension Fund is fed by appropriations out of the surplus of the Railways, whereas the Capital Fund is charged to the working expenses of the Railways
options.B: The Pension Fund and the Capital Fund are both fed by appropriations out of the surplus and are distinguished only by the works they finance
options.C: The Pension Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue and meets the pensionary benefits of the staff covered under the old pension scheme, whereas the Capital Fund is fed by appropriations out of the surplus (net revenue) and finances asset-creating capital works out of the Railways' internal resources
options.D: The Pension Fund finances capital works out of internal resources, whereas the Capital Fund meets the pensionary benefits of retired staff

e: The Pension Fund is fed by appropriations from revenue charged to working expenses and pays pensionary benefits under the old pension scheme. The Capital Fund is fed out of surplus and finances capital works from internal resources.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The first batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants during a financial year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the Monsoon Session.
2. The third and last batch of Supplementary Demands for Grants during a financial year is ordinarily presented to Parliament in the Budget Session.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both are correct in the normal budget calendar: the first batch of Supplementary Demands is presented in the Monsoon Session, and the third and final batch in the Budget Session of the same financial year.

q: The original appropriation for a charged service for a year is Rs 240 crore. During the year, charged provision of Rs 18 crore is surrendered and the Final Appropriation for the service works out to Rs 262 crore. The supplementary appropriation obtained for the service during the year is:

options.A: Rs 22 crore
options.B: Rs 58 crore
options.C: Rs 40 crore
options.D: Rs 4 crore

e: Final Appropriation = Original + Supplementary - Surrender, so Supplementary = 262 - 240 + 18 = Rs 40 crore for the charged service.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Special Railway Safety Fund (SRSF) from the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: The SRSF is a continuing fund fed out of the surplus of the Railways, whereas the Development Fund was a one-time fund set up in 2001-02
options.B: The SRSF is used for works of passenger amenities and labour welfare, whereas the Development Fund is used to wipe out arrears of renewal of over-aged safety assets
options.C: The SRSF and the Development Fund are both one-time funds, distinguished only by the year in which each was set up
options.D: The SRSF was a one-time fund set up in 2001-02 to wipe out the arrears of renewal and replacement of over-aged safety-related assets, whereas the Development Fund is fed by appropriations out of the surplus and is used for passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvement works

e: The Special Railway Safety Fund was a one-time fund of 2001-02 to wipe out arrears of renewal of over-aged safety assets. The Development Fund is fed out of surplus for passenger amenities, labour welfare and operational improvement works.

q: The revenue receipts of the Government for a year are Rs 19,80,000 crore and its revenue deficit for the year is Rs 4,20,000 crore. The revenue expenditure of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 24,00,000 crore
options.B: Rs 15,60,000 crore
options.C: Rs 23,80,000 crore
options.D: Rs 20,40,000 crore

e: Revenue expenditure = Revenue receipts + Revenue deficit = Rs 19,80,000 crore + Rs 4,20,000 crore = Rs 24,00,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Budget document 'Key Features of Budget' from 'Budget at a Glance'?

options.A: 'Key Features of Budget' presents the receipts and disbursements of the year under the Major Heads of account, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' explains the terms used in the Budget documents
options.B: 'Key Features of Budget' contains the detailed head-wise estimates of every Ministry, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' presents the highlights of the Budget proposals
options.C: 'Key Features of Budget' presents the highlights and salient features of the Budget proposals in a nutshell, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' presents a brief summary of the Budget, showing the receipts, the expenditure and the various deficit indicators in a nutshell
options.D: 'Key Features of Budget' is presented shortly before the Budget, whereas 'Budget at a Glance' is laid before Parliament after the Appropriation Act is passed

e: Key Features of Budget gives the highlights and salient features of the Budget proposals in a nutshell. Budget at a Glance summarises receipts, expenditure and deficit indicators in brief tabular form.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Finance Commission is constituted by the President at the expiration of every fifth year, or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary.
2. The Railway Convention Committee is a standing committee of Parliament which is constituted afresh every year.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is correct under Article 280: the Finance Commission is constituted by the President every fifth year or earlier if necessary. Statement 2 is wrong: the Railway Convention Committee is constituted periodically, not afresh every year.

q: A Bill which, if enacted, would involve expenditure from the Consolidated Fund of India, but which contains none of the matters specified in Article 110(1) of the Constitution, is introduced in the Rajya Sabha and is passed by both Houses without the President having recommended its consideration by either House. The correct position is that the Bill:

options.A: Is validly passed, since such a Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament
options.B: Cannot be passed by either House unless the President has recommended its consideration by that House
options.C: Required the President's recommendation only for its introduction, and not for its consideration
options.D: Could be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, the Rajya Sabha having no power to consider it at any stage

e: Such a Bill is a second-category Financial Bill under Article 117(3). It can be introduced in either House, but it cannot be passed by a House unless the President has recommended its consideration by that House.

q: The Effective Revenue Deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 2,10,000 crore and the grants-in-aid given during the year for the creation of capital assets amount to Rs 45,000 crore. The revenue deficit of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 1,65,000 crore
options.B: Rs 2,40,000 crore
options.C: Rs 2,10,000 crore
options.D: Rs 2,55,000 crore

e: Revenue deficit = Effective Revenue Deficit + Grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets = Rs 2,10,000 crore + Rs 45,000 crore = Rs 2,55,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Explanatory Memorandum' from the 'Notes on Demands for Grants' presented with the Budget?

options.A: The Explanatory Memorandum explains, for the information of Parliament, the proposals and estimates contained in the Railway Budget, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants explain the nature, scope and reasons for the significant provisions made in the Demands for Grants
options.B: The Explanatory Memorandum explains, clause by clause, the provisions of the Finance Bill, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants present a summary of the receipts and expenditure of the Government
options.C: The Explanatory Memorandum is a document of the Ministry of Finance alone, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants are prepared by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India
options.D: The Explanatory Memorandum presents the highlights of the Budget proposals, whereas the Notes on Demands for Grants exhibit the estimates in detail, head-wise

e: The Explanatory Memorandum explains the Railway Budget proposals and estimates for the information of Parliament, while the Notes on Demands for Grants explain the nature, scope and reasons for the significant provisions made in each Demand.

q: Through-traffic earnings are apportioned among Railways X, Y and Z in proportion to the distances travelled over them, namely 540 km, 360 km and 300 km respectively. The share falling to Railway X is Rs 5,400. The total through-traffic earnings apportioned are:
e: Total distance is 540 + 360 + 300 = 1200 km. Railway X share is 540 / 1200 of the total, so total earnings = Rs 5,400 x 1200 / 540 = Rs 12,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Deposits received by the Railways which remain unclaimed for more than three years are treated as lapsed deposits and credited to the revenue of the Railways.
2. A cheque issued by the Railways remains valid for payment for three months from the date of its issue.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. Deposits unclaimed for more than three years are treated as lapsed deposits and credited to railway revenue, and a railway cheque remains valid for payment for three months from its date of issue.

q: The opening balance under 'Manufacturing Suspense' of a railway, representing the cost of jobs in progress, is Rs 110 lakh. During the year, jobs of Rs 560 lakh are charged to the head and the closing balance under the head is Rs 90 lakh. The value of the completed jobs transferred out of the head during the year is:

options.A: Rs 540 lakh
options.B: Rs 620 lakh
options.C: Rs 560 lakh
options.D: Rs 580 lakh

e: Completed jobs transferred out = opening balance + jobs charged - closing balance = Rs 110 lakh + Rs 560 lakh - Rs 90 lakh = Rs 580 lakh.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Macro-Economic Framework Statement from the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act?

options.A: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement sets out three-year rolling targets for specified fiscal indicators, whereas the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement sets out the strategic priorities of the Government in the fiscal area
options.B: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement sets out an assessment of the growth prospects of the economy along with the specific underlying assumptions, whereas the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement sets out the expenditure projections of the Ministries for three years
options.C: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement is presented in the Session following the Budget Session, whereas the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement is presented along with the Budget
options.D: The Macro-Economic Framework Statement explains the provisions of the Finance Bill, whereas the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement presents the highlights of the Budget proposals

e: Under the FRBM Act, the Macro-Economic Framework Statement assesses growth prospects with its underlying assumptions, while the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement gives the three-year expenditure projections of the Ministries.

q: After the Demands for Grants for the full year have been voted, an Accounts Officer treats the amount earlier granted through a Vote on Account as an authorisation additional to the full grant for the year, and allows expenditure against both. This treatment is:

options.A: Incorrect — the amount granted through a Vote on Account forms part of the total grant for the year and is merged in it when the full grant is voted
options.B: Correct — a Vote on Account is a separate grant which remains available in addition to the full grant
options.C: Incorrect — a Vote on Account lapses only at the close of the financial year and can be used for charged expenditure alone
options.D: Correct — provided the total expenditure remains within the amount specified in the Schedule to the Appropriation Act for charged items

e: A Vote on Account is an advance grant for part of the year. When the full Demands are voted, the amount already granted on account is merged in the total grant for the year and is not an additional authorisation.

q: The fiscal deficit of the Government for a year is Rs 12,00,000 crore, its revenue receipts are Rs 26,00,000 crore and its non-debt capital receipts are Rs 1,50,000 crore. The total expenditure of the Government for the year is:

options.A: Rs 40,50,000 crore
options.B: Rs 37,50,000 crore
options.C: Rs 36,50,000 crore
options.D: Rs 39,50,000 crore

e: Fiscal deficit = total expenditure - revenue receipts - non-debt capital receipts. So total expenditure = Rs 12,00,000 crore + Rs 26,00,000 crore + Rs 1,50,000 crore = Rs 39,50,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Objectionable Item Register from the Liability Register maintained in the Accounts Office?

options.A: The Objectionable Item Register records the liabilities and commitments incurred against a grant, whereas the Liability Register watches the items held under objection during internal check
options.B: The Objectionable Item Register and the Liability Register are two names for the same register maintained for watching suspense outstandings
options.C: The Objectionable Item Register shows the balances outstanding under the debt and remittance heads, whereas the Liability Register records the sanctions and progressive expenditure on each work
options.D: The Objectionable Item Register watches items of expenditure or receipts held under objection during internal check till they are regularised, whereas the Liability Register records the liabilities and commitments incurred, such as orders and contracts placed, against which payments have yet to be made

e: The Objectionable Item Register watches items held under objection during internal check till regularised, while the Liability Register records liabilities and commitments such as orders and contracts placed against which payment is yet to be made.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. A Vote on Account normally authorises expenditure for a period of about six months of the financial year.
2. Ways and Means Advances made by the Reserve Bank of India to the Government are repayable not later than three months from the date of making the advance.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong because a Vote on Account normally covers about two months, not six months. Statement 2 is correct because Ways and Means Advances from the RBI are repayable not later than three months from the date of the advance.

q: Through-traffic earnings of Rs 27,000 include terminal charges which are retained by Railway P, the railway rendering the terminal services. The balance is apportioned between Railway P, over which the traffic travels 600 km, and Railway Q, over which it travels 400 km, in proportion to the distance travelled. The total amount falling to the share of Railway P, including the terminal charges retained by it, is Rs 17,400. The terminal charges are:
e: Let terminal charges be T. Balance apportioned is Rs 27,000 - T, of which P gets 600 / 1000. So T + 0.6 x (27,000 - T) = Rs 17,400, giving 0.4T = Rs 1,200 and T = Rs 3,000.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes DF-II from DF-III of the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: DF-II finances labour welfare works, whereas DF-III finances unremunerative operational improvement works
options.B: DF-II finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities, whereas DF-III finances labour welfare works
options.C: DF-II finances unremunerative operational improvement works, whereas DF-III finances works of passenger amenities
options.D: DF-II and DF-III are both sub-divisions financing works of road safety at level crossings and road bridges

e: In the Development Fund, DF-II finances labour welfare works, while DF-III finances unremunerative operational improvement works. Passenger and other railway user amenities are financed from DF-I, and safety works from DF-IV.

q: The opening debit balance under the head 'Cheques and Bills' of a railway is Rs 74,000. During the month, cheques and bills of Rs 6,90,000 are deposited with the bank and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 94,000. The amount of cheques and bills realised by the bank during the month is:
e: Realised by bank = opening balance + deposits - closing balance = Rs 74,000 + Rs 6,90,000 - Rs 94,000 = Rs 6,70,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Public Accounts Committee of Parliament was first set up in the year 1950.
2. The Estimates Committee of Parliament was first constituted in the year 1950.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong because the Public Accounts Committee was first set up in 1921. Statement 2 is correct because the Estimates Committee was first constituted in 1950, so only statement 2 holds.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes an 'Excess Grant' from a 'token grant'?

options.A: An Excess Grant is a nominal grant taken during the year for a new service, whereas a token grant is voted after the close of the year to regularise excess expenditure
options.B: An Excess Grant is voted after the close of the financial year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of a grant, whereas a token grant is a nominal grant taken during the year to obtain the approval of Parliament for a new service whose cost can be met by re-appropriation within the grant
options.C: An Excess Grant and a token grant are both taken during the year, the former for additional funds and the latter for a new service
options.D: An Excess Grant is granted by the Railway Board, whereas a token grant is granted by the Ministry of Finance

e: An Excess Grant is voted after the close of the year to regularise expenditure already incurred in excess of a grant. A token grant is a nominal grant taken during the year for a new service whose cost is met by re-appropriation within the grant.

q: The capital expenditure of the Government for a year is Rs 4,35,000 crore and its Effective Capital Expenditure for the year is Rs 5,10,000 crore. The grants-in-aid given during the year for the creation of capital assets amount to:

options.A: Rs 60,000 crore
options.B: Rs 90,000 crore
options.C: Rs 75,000 crore
options.D: Rs 45,000 crore

e: Effective Capital Expenditure = capital expenditure + grants-in-aid for creation of capital assets. So grants = Rs 5,10,000 crore - Rs 4,35,000 crore = Rs 75,000 crore.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'internal check' from 'appropriation audit' in relation to railway expenditure?

options.A: Internal check is conducted by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India after the expenditure is incurred, whereas appropriation audit is exercised by the Accounts Department before payment
options.B: Internal check and appropriation audit are both exercised by the Accounts Department at the pre-payment stage
options.C: Internal check verifies that the moneys disbursed were legally available for the purposes granted by Parliament, whereas appropriation audit is an integral part of the accounting system itself
options.D: Internal check is an integral part of the accounting system, exercised by the Accounts Department at the pre-payment stage before bills are passed for payment, whereas appropriation audit is conducted on behalf of the Comptroller and Auditor General of India to verify that the moneys disbursed were legally available for, and applied to, the services and purposes for which the grants and appropriations were made by Parliament

e: Internal check is part of the accounting system itself, exercised by the Accounts Department before payment. Appropriation audit, done for the CAG, verifies that moneys disbursed were legally available for and applied to the purposes granted by Parliament.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement, required to be laid before Parliament under the FRBM Act, is presented along with the Budget in the Budget Session itself.
2. The Economic Survey, reviewing the state of the economy, is presented to Parliament shortly before the presentation of the Union Budget.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Statement 1 is wrong because the Medium-Term Expenditure Framework Statement is presented in the session following the Budget Session, not with the Budget. Statement 2 is correct because the Economic Survey is presented shortly before the Union Budget.

q: The opening debit balance under the suspense head 'Demands Recoverable' of a railway is Rs 3,40,000. During the year, Rs 10,10,000 are realised from outside parties and credited to the head, and the closing debit balance under the head is Rs 2,90,000. The amounts debited to the head during the year for services rendered to outside parties are:
e: Debits = closing balance + realisations - opening balance = Rs 2,90,000 + Rs 10,10,000 - Rs 3,40,000 = Rs 9,60,000.

q: A station master, faced with an urgent local bill, pays it out of the day's earnings collected at the station and remits only the balance to the bank. This course is:

options.A: Permissible, provided the amount so spent is reported to the Cash Office on the same day
options.B: Permissible, provided the bill is one which the station master is competent to sanction
options.C: Not permissible — the earnings collected at a station are required to be remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank, and not utilised for local expenditure
options.D: Not permissible only where the amount spent exceeds the imprest held by the station master

e: Station earnings must be remitted in full to the Cash Office or the accredited bank. They cannot be used for local expenditure, however urgent or small the bill may be.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Classified Abstract' from the 'Suspense Register' of a railway?

options.A: The Classified Abstract watches the outstanding items under each suspense head, whereas the Suspense Register is the head-wise summary of the month's transactions
options.B: The Classified Abstract is a statement of the balances of the Ledger accounts, whereas the Suspense Register is compiled from the General Books and rendered to the Railway Board
options.C: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary of transactions, compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted, whereas the Suspense Register watches, item-wise, the amounts outstanding under each suspense head till they are cleared to the final heads of account
options.D: The Classified Abstract and the Suspense Register are both prepared only at the close of the financial year

e: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary of transactions compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted. The Suspense Register watches item-wise outstandings under each suspense head till clearance.

q: The opening credit balance under the head 'Demands Payable' of a railway is Rs 3,85,000. During the year, payments of Rs 12,60,000 are made and debited to the head, and the closing credit balance under the head is Rs 4,45,000. The amounts credited to the head during the year for goods and services received are:
e: Credits = closing balance + payments - opening balance = Rs 4,45,000 + Rs 12,60,000 - Rs 3,85,000 = Rs 13,20,000.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Special Railway Safety Fund was created on the recommendations of the Railway Safety Review Committee (Khanna Committee).
2. On the closure of the Special Railway Safety Fund in the year 2008, its unspent balance was transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways.
Which of the statements is/are correct?

options.A: 1 only
options.B: 2 only
options.C: Both 1 and 2
options.D: Neither 1 nor 2

e: Both statements are correct. The Special Railway Safety Fund was created on the Khanna Committee recommendations, and on its closure in 2008 its unspent balance was transferred to the Depreciation Reserve Fund.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Revenue Budget of the Railways from its Earnings Budget?

options.A: The Revenue Budget comprises the estimates of earnings and of working expenditure, including the appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund and the Pension Fund which form part of the working expenses, whereas the Earnings Budget contains only the estimates of the earnings expected from coaching, goods and sundry other traffic, framed on the basis of the traffic anticipated
options.B: The Revenue Budget contains the provision for the capital outlay on works, whereas the Earnings Budget contains the estimates of working expenditure
options.C: The Revenue Budget is framed by the executive departments alone, whereas the Earnings Budget is framed by the Railway Board alone
options.D: The Revenue Budget and the Earnings Budget are two names for the same component of the Railway Budget

e: The Revenue Budget covers earnings and working expenditure, including appropriations to the DRF and Pension Fund. The Earnings Budget covers only expected coaching, goods and sundry earnings based on anticipated traffic.

q: The annual allotment for a head of account is Rs 1,850 crore and the proportionate allotment available for a period of the year is Rs 740 crore. The budget proportion fixed for the period is:

options.A: 35 per cent
options.B: 40 per cent
options.C: 45 per cent
options.D: 30 per cent

e: Budget proportion = proportionate allotment / annual allotment x 100 = Rs 740 crore / Rs 1,850 crore x 100 = 40 per cent.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'bank scroll' from the 'Debt Head Report' of a railway?

options.A: The bank scroll is a monthly statement showing the balances under the debt heads, whereas the Debt Head Report is the daily statement rendered by the accredited bank
options.B: The bank scroll is maintained in the Cash & Pay Office to record cash receipts chronologically, whereas the Debt Head Report is rendered by the accredited bank for reconciliation
options.C: The bank scroll and the Debt Head Report are both rendered by the Railway Board from the Account Currents of the zonal railways
options.D: The bank scroll is the daily statement of receipts and payments rendered by the accredited bank, from which the bank's transactions are reconciled with the railway books, whereas the Debt Head Report is the monthly statement showing the balances outstanding under the debt, suspense and remittance heads, as recorded in the General Books

e: The bank scroll is the daily statement of receipts and payments rendered by the accredited bank for reconciliation with railway books. The Debt Head Report is the monthly statement of balances under debt, suspense and remittance heads in the General Books.

q: In a year governed by the Separation Convention of 1924, the contribution paid by the Railways to the General Revenues, in addition to the fixed dividend on the Capital-at-charge, amounts to Rs 260 crore, the contribution being one-fifth of the surplus profits of the Railways. The surplus profits of the Railways for the year are:

options.A: Rs 1,300 crore
options.B: Rs 1,040 crore
options.C: Rs 1,560 crore
options.D: Rs 2,600 crore

e: The additional contribution is one-fifth of surplus profits. So surplus profits = Rs 260 crore x 5 = Rs 1,300 crore under the Separation Convention of 1924.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes 'Unpaid Wages' from 'Deposits' in railway accounts?

options.A: 'Unpaid Wages' represents amounts received from outside parties which are repayable to them, whereas 'Deposits' represents wages drawn but remaining undisbursed
options.B: 'Unpaid Wages' represents wages and salaries drawn but remaining undisbursed to the staff entitled to them, held pending disbursement or claim, whereas 'Deposits' represents amounts received from parties, such as earnest money and security deposits, which are held by the Railways and are repayable or adjustable to the parties concerned
options.C: 'Unpaid Wages' is a suspense head pending apportionment among railways, whereas 'Deposits' is a remittance head in the course of settlement with the Reserve Bank
options.D: 'Unpaid Wages' and 'Deposits' are both heads under which traffic earnings are held pending apportionment

e: Unpaid Wages are wages and salaries drawn but remaining undisbursed to the staff entitled to them. Deposits are amounts received from parties, such as earnest money and security deposits, held repayable or adjustable to them.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the Final Modification Estimates stage of the budget cycle of a railway?

options.A: The Final Grant is settled — the actuals of the first nine months are compiled — savings are surrendered — funds are re-appropriated within the grant
options.B: Savings are surrendered before the grant is voted — the Appropriation Act is passed — the actuals of nine months are compiled — the Final Grant is settled
options.C: Funds are re-appropriated from one grant to another — savings are surrendered to Parliament — the Final Grant is settled — the actuals of nine months are compiled
options.D: The actuals of the first nine months are compiled — the savings foreseen are surrendered and the additional requirements assessed — funds are re-appropriated within the grant to the heads requiring them — the Final Grant for the year is settled

e: At Final Modification, nine months actuals are compiled first, foreseen savings are surrendered and additional needs assessed, funds are re-appropriated within the grant, and then the Final Grant for the year is settled.

q: The Block Account of a railway at the commencement of a year stands at Rs 56,000 crore. The capital outlay incurred during the year is Rs 3,800 crore and the Block Account at the close of the year stands at Rs 59,100 crore. The original cost of the assets sold and removed from the Block during the year is:

options.A: Rs 900 crore
options.B: Rs 500 crore
options.C: Rs 1,100 crore
options.D: Rs 700 crore

e: Assets removed = opening Block + capital outlay - closing Block = Rs 56,000 crore + Rs 3,800 crore - Rs 59,100 crore = Rs 700 crore.

q: Which of the following is the correct sequence in the accounting of a deposit work executed by the Railways for an outside party?

options.A: The party deposits the estimated cost of the work — the amount is credited to the 'Deposits' head — the expenditure incurred on the work is debited to the 'Deposits' head as the work progresses — on completion, the unspent balance is refunded to the party by debit to the 'Deposits' head
options.B: The expenditure on the work is charged to the revenues of the Railways — the party deposits the cost on completion — the deposit is credited to revenue — the balance is adjusted through the Works Register
options.C: The amount deposited by the party is credited to the earnings of the Railways — the expenditure is debited to the 'Deposits' head — the unspent balance is credited to the Depreciation Reserve Fund
options.D: The work is included in the Works Programme (Pink Book) — budget provision is made for it — the party's deposit is treated as a supplementary grant — the expenditure is watched through the Budget Register

e: For a deposit work, the party deposits the estimated cost, the amount is credited to Deposits, expenditure as incurred is debited to Deposits, and on completion the unspent balance is refunded by debit to Deposits.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes DF-I from DF-III of the Development Fund of the Railways?

options.A: DF-I finances labour welfare works, whereas DF-III finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities
options.B: DF-I finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities, whereas DF-III finances unremunerative operational improvement works
options.C: DF-I finances unremunerative operational improvement works, whereas DF-III finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities
options.D: DF-I and DF-III are both sub-divisions financing works of road safety at level crossings and road bridges

e: In the Development Fund, DF-I finances works of passenger and other railway user amenities, while DF-III finances unremunerative operational improvement works. Labour welfare works fall under DF-II.

q: The opening credit balance under the 'Deposits' head of a railway is Rs 4,60,000. During the year, deposits of Rs 13,80,000 are received from contractors and other parties and credited to the head, and deposits of Rs 10,95,000 are repaid or adjusted and debited to the head. The closing balance under the head is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 7,45,000
options.B: A credit balance of Rs 29,35,000
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 7,45,000
options.D: A credit balance of Rs 8,45,000

e: Closing balance = opening credit Rs 4,60,000 + deposits received Rs 13,80,000 - repaid or adjusted Rs 10,95,000 = a credit balance of Rs 7,45,000.

q: A zonal railway holds, for the information of Parliament, two documents relating to the Budget. In the first document, the proposals and estimates contained in the Railway Budget are explained; the second document explains, clause by clause, the provisions contained in the Finance Bill. The two documents are respectively:

options.A: The Explanatory Memorandum and the Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill
options.B: The Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill and the Explanatory Memorandum
options.C: The Notes on Demands for Grants and the Explanatory Memorandum
options.D: The Explanatory Memorandum and the Notes on Demands for Grants

e: The document explaining the Budget proposals and estimates is the Explanatory Memorandum. The document explaining the Finance Bill clause by clause is the Memorandum Explaining the Provisions in the Finance Bill.

q: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission of India are shown by a clerk in a list of expenditure charged on the Consolidated Fund of India. The treatment shown by the clerk is:

options.A: Correct, because the Election Commission is a constitutional body
options.B: Correct, because all expenses of constitutional bodies are charged
options.C: Incorrect, because such expenses are met out of the Contingency Fund of India
options.D: Incorrect, because the administrative expenses of the Election Commission are voted by Parliament as part of the Demands for Grants

e: The administrative expenses of the Election Commission are voted expenditure, forming part of the Demands for Grants. Only specified items like the salaries of the Election Commissioners are charged on the Consolidated Fund.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Depreciation Reserve Fund from the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh of the Railways?

options.A: The Depreciation Reserve Fund finances safety-related works, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh finances the renewal and replacement of railway assets generally
options.B: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is financed wholly by Gross Budgetary Support, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh is charged to the working expenses of the Railways
options.C: The Depreciation Reserve Fund is credited with appropriations from revenue, assessed with reference to the original cost and codal life of assets, for renewal and replacement of assets, whereas the Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh finances safety-related works out of Gross Budgetary Support and the Railways' internal resources
options.D: Both the funds are credited with the safety surcharge levied on passenger fares

e: The DRF is credited with appropriations from revenue based on original cost and codal life of assets for renewal and replacement. The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh finances safety works from Gross Budgetary Support and internal resources.

q: An asset of the Railways has an original cost of Rs 3,60,000 and a prescribed (codal) life of 40 years. Appropriations to the Depreciation Reserve Fund being assessed with reference to the original cost of the asset and its codal life, the annual appropriation on account of this asset works out to:
e: Annual DRF appropriation = original cost / codal life = Rs 3,60,000 / 40 = Rs 9,000.

q: In the books of the Railway Board, the inter-railway transfer transactions of the zonal railways are finally adjusted under a head, while a debit raised by one railway against another railway in such a transaction is intimated to it through a document. The head and the document are respectively:

options.A: 'Transfer Railways' and the Transfer Certificate
options.B: The Transfer Certificate and 'Transfer Railways'
options.C: 'Transfer Railways' and the Cash Remittance Note
options.D: PAO Suspense and the Transfer Certificate

e: Inter-railway transfer transactions are finally adjusted in the Railway Board books under Transfer Railways, and a debit raised by one railway against another is intimated through a Transfer Certificate.

q: A private member of the Lok Sabha seeks to introduce a Money Bill in the House. The correct position is that:

options.A: A private member can introduce a Money Bill with the permission of the Speaker
options.B: A private member can introduce a Money Bill if it is recommended by the President
options.C: A Money Bill can be introduced only by the Leader of the House
options.D: A Money Bill can be introduced only by a Minister, that is, it can only be a Government Bill

e: A Money Bill can be introduced only by a Minister as a Government Bill, and only in the Lok Sabha with the recommendation of the President. A private member cannot introduce a Money Bill.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Classified Abstract' from the 'Ledger' in the books of a railway?

options.A: The Classified Abstract is the principal book from which the Trial Balance is extracted, whereas the Ledger is a head-wise monthly summary of transactions
options.B: The Classified Abstract is maintained by the executive departments, whereas the Ledger is maintained by the Traffic Accounts Office
options.C: The Classified Abstract and the Ledger are two names for the same book of account
options.D: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary of transactions compiled from the subsidiary books, from which the General Books are posted, whereas the Ledger is the principal book maintaining accounts for all the heads of account, its postings being made from the closing totals of the Journal and the Classified Abstract

e: The Classified Abstract is the head-wise monthly summary compiled from subsidiary books from which the General Books are posted. The Ledger is the principal book for all heads, posted from the closing totals of the Journal and Classified Abstract.

q: The total lease charges payable by the Railways to the Indian Railway Finance Corporation for a year are Rs 11,400 crore, of which the interest (finance charge) component is Rs 4,650 crore. The capital (principal) component of the lease charges for the year is:

options.A: Rs 7,250 crore
options.B: Rs 6,750 crore
options.C: Rs 6,250 crore
options.D: Rs 16,050 crore

e: Capital component = total lease charges - interest component = Rs 11,400 crore - Rs 4,650 crore = Rs 6,750 crore payable to IRFC.

q: The declared provisions of a Finance Bill, relating to certain duties, have taken effect immediately on the introduction of the Bill under a statute enacted for the provisional collection of taxes. That statute is:

options.A: The Finance Act of the year concerned
options.B: The Appropriation Act of the year concerned
options.C: The Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931
options.D: The General Clauses Act, 1897

e: Declared provisions of a Finance Bill take immediate effect on introduction under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, which gives provisional force of law to the proposed tax changes.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Journal Book' from the 'Main Cash Book' of a railway?

options.A: The Journal Book records all cash receipts and payments chronologically, whereas the Main Cash Book records all transfer entries
options.B: All transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded in the Journal Book, whereas all cash receipts and payments effected through the Cash & Pay Office are recorded chronologically in the Main Cash Book
options.C: The Journal Book is a General Book, whereas the Main Cash Book is maintained by the executive departments
options.D: The Journal Book is maintained only at the close of the year, whereas the Main Cash Book is maintained only in the Traffic Accounts Office

e: All transfer and adjustment entries are first recorded in the Journal Book. All cash receipts and payments through the Cash and Pay Office are recorded chronologically in the Main Cash Book.

q: A Finance Bill introduced in the Lok Sabha along with the Budget remains pending before Parliament for a considerable time after its introduction. Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, the Bill must be passed by Parliament within:

options.A: 30 days of its introduction
options.B: 45 days of its introduction
options.C: 60 days of its introduction
options.D: 75 days of its introduction

e: Under the Provisional Collection of Taxes Act, 1931, a Finance Bill to which a declaration applies must be passed by Parliament within 75 days of its introduction, failing which the declaration ceases to have effect.

q: An executive department proposes that, in the Detailed Demands for Grants, the estimates of expenditure be shown after netting off the recoveries expected under the head, so that only the net requirement is exhibited. The correct position is that the estimates in the Detailed Demands for Grants are exhibited:

options.A: On a gross basis, the recoveries being shown separately as 'Deduct' entries to arrive at the net amount of the Demand
options.B: Net of all recoveries, the recoveries not being shown at all
options.C: Only for the charged portion of the expenditure
options.D: Only in terms of the net cash outgo from the Consolidated Fund of India

e: Detailed Demands for Grants are exhibited on a gross basis. Recoveries are shown separately as Deduct entries below the gross estimates to arrive at the net amount of the Demand, and are not netted off at the head level.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the 'Receipts Budget' from 'Budget at a Glance', the two documents presented with the Union Budget?

options.A: The Receipts Budget is a brief summary of the Budget showing the deficit indicators, whereas Budget at a Glance presents a detailed analysis of the revenues and capital receipts
options.B: Both the documents present only the receipts of the Government, in summary and in detail respectively
options.C: The Receipts Budget presents a detailed analysis of the tax revenues, non-tax revenues and capital receipts of the Government, whereas Budget at a Glance presents a brief summary of the Budget, showing the receipts, expenditure and the various deficit indicators
options.D: The Receipts Budget is presented only to the Rajya Sabha, whereas Budget at a Glance is presented only to the Lok Sabha

e: The Receipts Budget gives a detailed analysis of tax revenues, non-tax revenues and capital receipts. Budget at a Glance gives a brief summary of receipts, expenditure and the various deficit indicators.

q: In classifying a receipt of the Railways for which no specific minor head is provided in the List of Major and Minor Heads of Account, an Accounts Officer proposes to use the minor head bearing the code '800'. The proposal is:

options.A: Incorrect, because the code '800' is reserved for suspense transactions
options.B: Correct, because the minor head '800' is generally used for 'Other receipts' or 'Other expenditure' not covered by any specific minor head
options.C: Incorrect, because the code '800' stands for Deposits with the Reserve Bank
options.D: Incorrect, because receipts without a specific minor head are credited to the Contingency Fund of India

e: Where no specific minor head is provided in the List of Major and Minor Heads, minor head 800 is generally used for Other Receipts or Other Expenditure, so the proposal is correct.

q: The opening debit balance under the suspense head 'Miscellaneous Advances' of a railway is Rs 2,85,000. During the year, advances of Rs 9,40,000 are made and debited to the head, and advances of Rs 8,15,000 are recovered or adjusted and credited to the head. The closing balance under the head is:

options.A: A debit balance of Rs 4,10,000
options.B: A debit balance of Rs 3,10,000
options.C: A credit balance of Rs 4,10,000
options.D: A debit balance of Rs 20,40,000

e: Closing balance = opening debit Rs 2,85,000 + advances made Rs 9,40,000 - recovered Rs 8,15,000 = a debit balance of Rs 4,10,000.

q: Which of the following correctly distinguishes the Gender Budget Statement from the Outcome Budget presented with the Union Budget?

options.A: The Gender Budget Statement relates the financial outlays provided to the physical outcomes expected, whereas the Outcome Budget reflects the allocations flowing to women
options.B: The Gender Budget Statement has been presented since 2005-06 and separately reflects the schemes with full allocation for women and the schemes in which at least 30 per cent of the allocation flows to women, whereas the Outcome Budget relates the financial outlays provided to the physical outcomes and deliverables expected from them
options.C: Both the statements were first introduced in the Budget for 2017-18, on the merger of the Railway Budget with the General Budget
options.D: The Gender Budget Statement is a statement of the Railways alone, whereas the Outcome Budget covers all the Ministries except the Railways

e: The Gender Budget Statement, presented since 2005-06, shows schemes fully for women and schemes where at least 30 per cent flows to women. The Outcome Budget links financial outlays to physical outcomes and deliverables expected.

q: In the Government accounts, the capital outlay on a railway work is Rs 1,000 crore, out of which Rs 350 crore is met from the Depreciation Reserve Fund of the Railways. In exhibiting the outlay under Major Head 5002, the portion met from the Fund is adjusted through minor heads styled as:

options.A: 'Transfer to Railway Funds'
options.B: 'Suspense — Railway Funds'
options.C: 'Recoveries on Capital Account'
options.D: 'Deduct — Amount met from' the respective Fund

e: Under Major Head 5002, capital outlay met from a Railway Fund is exhibited through Deduct - Amount met from the respective Fund minor heads, so that the net charge on Capital is shown correctly.

q: The allocation string of a track renewal work financed from the Depreciation Reserve Fund is written as 'DRF-3100'; had the same work been financed from Capital, the string would have been written as 'Capital-3100'. In these allocation strings, the portion appearing before the Plan Head number denotes:

options.A: The source of finance (fund) from which the work is financed
options.B: The zonal railway executing the work
options.C: The year in which the work was sanctioned
options.D: The Primary Unit of the work

e: In an allocation string such as DRF-3100 or Capital-3100, the portion before the Plan Head number 3100 denotes the source of finance, that is the fund or Capital, from which the work is financed.
